statements.impact_statement: PostgreSQL states that only major version 18 is affected by CVE-2026-120144 (PostgreSQL type-cache invalidation gap executes arbitrary code) and that versions before PostgreSQL 18 are unaffected: https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-120144/ and https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-120144. The 18.7 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/18.7/, describe the fix as replacing the type cache's in_progress_list mechanism. That mechanism is present in src/backend/utils/cache/typcache.c from REL_18_0 but absent from it at every PostgreSQL 17 release this owner publishes (REL_17_7 through REL_17_12; for example https://github.com/postgres/postgres/blob/REL_17_12/src/backend/utils/cache/typcache.c), and the 17.12 release notes do not list CVE-2026-120144. This owner publishes PostgreSQL 17 only: every published build for Alpine 3.23 (17.7-r0, 17.8-r0, 17.9-r0, 17.10-r0, 17.11-r0 and 17.12-r0) has a postgres server binary reporting that 17.x release on both x86_64 and aarch64, and none of the Alpine patches applied in the 17.12-r0 APKBUILD touch the type cache. Alpine's postgresql17 17.12-r0 secfixes list CVE-2026-120144 (https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/ce22298320177ae25085d86fbf3b4fc1150c16a2/main/postgresql17/APKBUILD), but upstream does not consider major version 17 affected.
